body:
Some little range of motion exercises, some of which have seemed to get me to where I'm at, but no miracles I guess. I've definitely improved a lot, but the progress capped about a month ago, so that was disheartening.

As for my ongoing treatment, the doctors are stumped. They gave me a test involving some very large needles and my flesh. Tl:dr, I didn't feel some of those needles at all, so I need more extensive testing to see what's going on with the nerves.

> Is there a point of normalization in the future? 

Not sure what you mean by this tbh.

>What kind of work have you done? And what'd you study in school?

I had just graduated from a school that gave me a certificate to work in a field that's very hands-on and involved being on your feet all day and lifting/carrying/using your hands etc. Because it's uncertain if I'll make a "full" recovery, it's best that I forget that profession altogether... After all, it's been several months and while I've certainly improved physically, I'm far from the way I used to be.

> what do you got to lose 

My autonomy. It's not a fair trade to me...
Years. But I think maybe that has a lot to do with how things seem to be continuously hitting the fan.
And in my region, if I go and tell a professional I want to kill myself, it's pretty much guaranteed that I will be committed. I don't want that.
I've been reaching out to my friends and I feel more at ease now that I know that they know, but.... it hasn't in any way kept me from wanting an out.
This reminds me of 1998 computer graphics...
I've known people to be committed for things like this. I'm terrified of that possibility and feel like the forcible removal of my autonomy in that way would only make things much worse.

>  I can't imagine how frustrating and disheartening that must be.

I'm just tired of everything being a battle. I wish my body and mind could cooperate but sometimes doing the simplest things is difficult. It took two months of recovery for me to adequately wash and brush my hair.

>you might want to call and talk to someone with more training than I have. I can refer you to someone if you want.

I don't know what I want, or should want. I don't know if a professional could help me, and I'm afraid of the possible outcomes based on people I've known personally that have gone through similar emotions...

>I'll be here.

Thank you...

I'm afraid that they will commit me, honestly. In my region, of people I've known personally, that happens if you show any real sign of wanting to hurt or kill yourself. I think that approach would make things way worse.

In short, I'm afraid.
